methodology_link.description: 2004 follow-up states that the second survey used almost the same technique as the 1999 survey: positive favorability and governing-ability evaluations combined with equal weight.
methodology_link.note: Do not copy the 2004 sample size, candidate count, survey firm, or error margin backward to 1999 without the 1999 primary issue.

direct_facts: 1999-07-01 issue no.264 contained the first 'next-generation leader' public-opinion survey.
Lee In-je was rank 3 in 1999 and rank 22 in 2004.
Chung Dong-young was rank 5 in 1999 and rank 6 in 2004.
The 2004 survey used almost the same favorability + governing-ability technique as the 1999 survey.

national_assembly_library_locator.retrieval_value: The exact issue is directly identified, so an issue scan should allow primary reconstruction of the full ranking/methodology if the table survives in print.

rejected_methods: Do not infer missing 1999 ranks from the 2002 Democratic primary order.
Do not borrow ranks from Shindonga, Newspeople, Ilyo Shinmun, KSOI, or other contemporary leadership polls.
Do not assume the 1999 candidate pool was 31 just because the 2004 survey used 31 candidates.
Do not infer rank from later presidential success.
